layer_at_fault_line: P2 is marked 'fixed' for being 'a definition, set by the owner' though 'not itself tested'; file 33's line 'Fixed - the owner put this part outside the test, and said so' reads as the document's own author (the one who set the definition) to a reader marking a document, rather than as the person who set this test's own fixed requirements.
quotes: test_remove: 'Remove it and a machine may cheat with infinite precision, which is exactly the failure being explained.' (P3); 'remove it and the hoped-for speed-up would stand.' (P9). test_swap: 'Swap in a discrete classical physics and the failure goes.' (P4). test_poke (NAME ONLY, only the would-alter half given): 'Poke: name a physically realizable system Q cannot simulate — the non-recursive-set device is the standing candidate; running it against an ordinary enumerator would tell.' test_flip: 'Had quantum physics also failed (1.2), the paper's machine would not be universal. The paper does not cover both outcomes: it says classical fails and why, quantum passes and why.' test_reverse (NAME ONLY, direction named, no separate poke of either end): 'Direction. It runs forward, from machine to simulated system, not backwards from a result.' test_hunt: '"Q simulates any finite system" leans on "finite-dimensional". That is stated openly, not smuggled: the universe's own case is left open.' test_addjob: 'Job: settle whether the universe's state space is finite (the Bekenstein bound), which currently carries P1 and P8 together.' test_rival / rivals_built basis: 'Benioff's machine and Feynman's simulator are the near neighbours, and are separated: Benioff's is effectively classical; Feynman's laws are handed over by fiat, not set by a program. A machine computing a non-recursive set is the change that would tell the principle from a rival.' test_patches: 'The superscattering set is broad, but comes with a gauge — the inequalities (3.12) and the open-set argument — so what it swallows can be watched.' test_inside (NAME ONLY, change named, nothing said about what it would show): 'Held by the claim that rival readings cannot say where the answer was computed — testable in principle by the experiment promised elsewhere.'
